transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-04-14 11:00 AM PT
- Duration: ~52 minutes
- Attendees: Lena Ortiz, Ben Cho (Redwood); Priya Nair, Evan Brooks, Joan Castillo, Samir Patel (Mistral)

Summary (auto): quick security review focused on what admin activity and audit telemetry Redwood captures, selectable export patterns (S3, syslog, webhook), KMS/envelope encryption options, and retention/immutable store for forensics readiness. Agreed to pilot S3 export + KMS envelopes and share playbook.

Topics: SOC 2 evidence, RBAC/SSO audit trails, admin console actions, export formats (json, ndjson), long-term retention, legal hold, HSM/KMS rotation, immutable object store, log lineage.

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena Ortiz: All right, hi everyone, thanks for taking the time. I'm Lena from Redwood, AE on the account, and Ben's our solutions engineer. How are you all?
[00:08] Priya Nair: Good morning, thanks. We wanted to be explicit about our forensics posture, what evidence we can pull if there's an incident and how long it stays.
[00:16] Ben Cho: Yeah totally, that's what this call is for. We'll walk through what we capture by default, optional admin telemetry, and the export/retention options. We'll also call out the encryption and KMS patterns.
[00:28] Evan Brooks: Quick note—Mistral has a 7 year retention minimum in some workflows, and legal hold can extend that. We're particularly worried about immutable bit rot and proof of tamper.
[00:37] Ben Cho: Understood. High level first: Redwood captures request/response metadata, token counts, model selection, model version, and admin actions like auth changes, RBAC grants, role edits, SSO config changes. We also capture route-level policy changes and rollout events.
[00:53] Joan Castillo: Do you capture user impersonation attempts or failed SAML assertions? That's one of our compliance checks.
[01:00] Ben Cho: Yes we log SAML/SSO auth outcomes, including assertion IDs, timestamps, and error codes. Occasionally the auto-transcript will miss exact SAML assertion names—so in the evidence export we include raw assertion references.
[01:14] Priya Nair: How about API key usage—rotate events and create/delete? We need a chain of custody for key material events.
[01:21] Lena Ortiz: We record API key lifecycle events: creation, last-used, revoke, rotate. We also surface token-level metadata in the admin console. For chain of custody, we can provide signed export manifest.
[01:33] Samir Patel: For ingest, do you stream to our VPC or push to our S3? We prefer S3 with server-side encryption but we want client-side envelope encryption with our KMS.
[01:42] Ben Cho: You can do both. We support direct push to customer S3 (cross-account) or you can have Redwood stream to an endpoint—syslog/HTTP webhook. For encryption, Redwood supports server-side encryption SSE-S3 and SSE-KMS, and we also support envelope encryption where Redwood encrypts with a per-customer data key that you wrap with your KMS. We call out HSM options in the private deployment.
[02:02] Evan Brooks: Is the envelope key wrapped with our KMS CMK or Redwood's?
[02:06] Ben Cho: For private and some enterprise customers, you can bring your own CMK and we wrap with that. For hosted accounts, default is Redwood-managed KMS unless BYOK is on contract. There was a tiny typo in an earlier doc, sometimes shows as "bring-your-own KM S" in the UI, but it's BYOK.
[02:21] Joan Castillo: What fields are included in the audit export? We need full admin verbatim, IP addresses, session IDs, before/after state for role edits.
[02:28] Ben Cho: Export payload includes timestamp, actor id/email, IP, user-agent, action type, target resource, before/after diffs (when applicable), request ID, model id, route id, and full response payload optionally. We can toggle to include anonymized PII redaction or keep full PII for forensics.
[02:46] Priya Nair: If we request redaction off, are there controls for retention? We don't want PII in long-term storage if legal doesn't require it.
[02:54] Lena Ortiz: We recommend scoped exports: per-regulatory workspace settings. You can configure exports to be anonymized by default then lift anonymization under legal hold.
[03:05] [crosstalk] Evan Brooks: And retention, what's the maximum?
[03:08] Ben Cho: There's no hard-coded maximum in our architecture; it's policy-driven. We ship exports to your S3 and from there you can set Object Lock with a retention period (governance or compliance mode) and lifecycle policies to transition to Glacier. Redwood can also retain a copy in cold storage if you contract for evidence retention add-on.
[03:25] Joan Castillo: About immutability—does Redwood support S3 Object Lock via the export path?
[03:30] Ben Cho: Yes, if you use cross-account S3 exports and enable Object Lock on the bucket, exports can be written with retention headers so they are immutable. For system-owned buckets we can offer an immutable store via our private deployment option.
[03:43] Priya Nair: Can we get signing of exports? We want cryptographic proof of export integrity for chain of custody.
[03:50] Ben Cho: We can include a signed manifest—HMAC or an RSA signature over a manifest file. For the highest assurance we can integrate with HSM-backed keys (YubiHSM, Cloud HSM) when on Private.
[04:03] Samir Patel: Any standard format? We want NDJSON with one event per line for easy querying.
[04:08] Ben Cho: NDJSON is the default for event exports. For bulk snapshots we can do compressed tar.gz of ndjson plus a JSON manifest with checksums.
[04:18] Evan Brooks: About the log retention policies—if we set a 7-year retention, costs look scary. Do you have guidance on binning events by TTL?
[04:26] Lena Ortiz: Yes—Redwood Optimize suggests tiering: keep high-fidelity admin and auth events for the full retention, but you can downsample model token-level telemetry after 90 days, or store only aggregates. We'll share a recommended binning table.
[04:41] Ben Cho: Also you can sample debug trace spans for a fraction of requests, or use prefix caching to avoid storing identical prompt history repeatedly.
[04:49] Joan Castillo: Does Redwood's SOC 2 report describe the evidence capture process? We need to reference that in audits.
[04:55] Lena Ortiz: Yes SOC 2 and ISO attestations include a section on audit logging and retention controls. We'll send the attestation and the evidence playbook link.
[05:04] [15:02] Priya Nair: Something to call out — we need deletion events and who authorized them, not just that a delete happened.
[05:10] Ben Cho: Delete events include actor, justification field, and request ID. We retain tombstone records even after object deletion if configured. That allows you to show a deletion event even if the associated artifacts are removed.
[05:24] Samir Patel: For streaming, how do you handle backpressure? If our S3 is throttled, can Redwood buffer?
[05:31] Ben Cho: Redwood buffers in an encrypted queue for a configurable TTL; if downstream is unavailable we can hold for X hours/days depending on contract, or route to a fallback bucket. We also support pushing to Kinesis or Kafka in your VPC for ingestion.
[05:45] Evan Brooks: Are there schema versions? We need stable field names for our SIEM parsing.
[05:50] Ben Cho: Events include a schema_version field and we support backward compatible evolution. We'll maintain a changelog and provide migration guidance.
[05:59] Joan Castillo: Can you show an example record?
[06:02] Ben Cho: Sure — (reads) {timestamp, actor, actor_email, actor_role, action: "rbac.role.update", target: "workspace:dev", before: {...}, after: {...}, request_id: "r-123", ip: "203.0.113.12", ua: "curl/7.68", schema_version: "v1.3"}.
[06:24] Priya Nair: On key rotation—if we rotate CMKs, how do you handle previously encrypted exports?
[06:30] Ben Cho: Wrapped keys are stored with key version metadata. During rotation, we include key id metadata so you can unwrapHistorical envelopes if you still have access to prior CMKs. For permanent key deletion, we recommend legal hold off until you rewrap or export decrypted copies if policy requires.
[06:48] [small gap, 06:48-07:05 noise]
[07:05] Samir Patel: Want to confirm the retention controls UI—can we scope by project tag or by route?
[07:12] Ben Cho: Yes, per-route and per-workspace retention settings are supported. You can tag routes with classifications (e.g., PHI, PII) and attach different retention lifecycles.
[07:23] Priya Nair: We also need to make sure audit exports are accessible to our IR team via cross-account role, not via a shared account.
[07:30] Ben Cho: Cross-account role with trust policy is the recommended pattern. We'll provide the trust policy example.
[07:38] Evan Brooks: Any SLA for export availability and time-to-delivery? If we request a 90-day legal-hold export, what's the throughput?
[07:45] Lena Ortiz: We'll include export SLAs in the addendum. For large backfills, the SE can provide throughput estimates and parallelization guidance.
[07:55] Joan Castillo: Forensics: do you capture model input/output payloads? That's sensitive.
[08:01] Ben Cho: We capture request and response payloads optionally. By default we store metadata and truncated payloads. You can opt-in to full payload capture for forensics, but we recommend encrypting and restricting those artifacts heavily.
[08:16] Priya Nair: Who has access within Redwood to production logs? Internal RBAC?
[08:21] Ben Cho: Access is restricted by role; SEs don't have broad access unless you grant it. We log all internal access and include an auditor role for customers to review.
[08:32] Evan Brooks: Competitors we looked at — Datadog and Splunk — but the unified inference + export patterns here are compelling.
[08:40] Lena Ortiz: Thanks, appreciate that.
[08:43] [15:00 minute mark note: mid-call recap]
[08:46] Lena Ortiz: Quick recap: Redwood will send the evidence playbook, examples for S3 cross-account export, the object lock pattern, and a sample NDJSON export. Mistral sends regs matrix and retention matrix. SE will run ingest sim.
[08:58] Priya Nair: On legal hold — can we trigger on a case ID and have exports preserved automatically?
[09:04] Ben Cho: Yes, we offer a legal-hold API where you can attach case IDs to exports to prevent lifecycle transitions. We'll demo that in the pilot.
[09:13] Samir Patel: About alerting — can we get telemetry that export jobs failed or were delayed?
[09:18] Ben Cho: Yes, export job statuses stream to your monitoring endpoint and we provide alerting hooks; you can also have webhook callbacks when jobs complete or fail.
[09:27] Joan Castillo: A couple of compliance specifics — SOC 2 requires retention evidence for six months of admin access reviews. Can Redwood produce the reviewer logs?
[09:35] Lena Ortiz: We can produce reviewer action logs and attestations showing who reviewed what and when.
[09:41] Priya Nair: One last thing, chain of custody: we want a signed timeline with checksums.
[09:47] Ben Cho: Manifest with checksums and signatures is standard we provide; we'll show both HMAC and RSA options.
[09:55] Lena Ortiz: Great. We'll follow up with the links and set up the pilot. Any final questions?
[10:00] Priya Nair: No, that's it for now — thank you.

End of transcript.
